notes: This contract pins Umbra's bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 asynchronous-delivery slice to the Requirements Lab's clauses 8.15.3 and 8.16.5. In the embedded in-process profile, a time-constrained federate defaults to synchronous receive-order delivery, may enable receive-order callbacks while idle, and returns to time-advance-only receive-order delivery when disabled. The integration scenario exercises both HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE: Enable Asynchronous Delivery and entering Time Advancing release deferred callbacks through the next Evoke call or directly during the service call, respectively. A regional receive-order companion proves the same gate around an overlap-qualified Send Interaction With Regions callback and preserves the source RegionHandle set across disable/re-enable. A separate Connection Lost integration uses the enabled state to receive the source-mandated receive-order HLAreportFederateLost while pairing its encoded cutoff with a timestamped application delivery; paired bounded DELETE_OBJECTS collisions prove post-grant receive-order cleanup becomes eligible in the same TAR after the cutoff reflection under both callback models. Neither widens this into generic MOM or timestamped-delivery behavior. A separate selected-filesystem case records each successful no-argument service with an empty supplied-argument list and Table 5's explicit [null] return form. Time-stamped delivery generally, remote transport, generic MOM reporting, save/restore persistence of deferred callbacks, package evidence, protected review, and conformance remain outside this slice.
